svg.title: Priority-routed compaction worker pools
svg.desc: Compaction jobs carry a priority hint. A router reads the .compactions file and dispatches jobs to differently-provisioned worker pools: a hot pool of small, fast workers handles L0 drain jobs to keep writers from stalling; a heavy pool of large workers handles big-tier compactions where throughput matters more than latency; a background pool of cheap spot instances handles low-priority maintenance work.
svg.text: Router · reads priority, dispatches to matching pool
workers in each pool poll only jobs they're configured to claim
Pools sized independently for cost ÷ latency tradeoff
Hot pool: small, always-on, on-demand instances · pay for guaranteed latency
Background pool: cheap spot instances · accept preemption for ~70% cost savings
L0 drain SLOs are isolated from heavy compactions — a big merge can't
starve the hot pool, since they don't share workers. Background pool
can vanish (spot reclaim) without affecting writers or readers.
Stateless workers + object storage as the coordination layer make
priority-aware compute provisioning a configuration concern, not a redesign.
